simple: A `DragDetector` lets players grab and move 3D things in your world, like opening a drawer, sliding a block, or spinning a wheel. Just put one inside a part or model and it becomes draggable with a mouse, touch, gamepad, or VR, with no code. You can choose how it moves (slide on a line, slide on the floor, or rotate), set limits, and choose whether it moves smoothly by physics. Scripts can react to dragging, for example dimming a light as a slider moves.
analogy: It is like putting a handle on a drawer. The handle lets you pull, and the drawer's rails decide which way it can go and how far.
keyPoints: Put a `DragDetector` directly inside a `Part`, `MeshPart`, or `Model` to make it draggable on any device.
In Studio, dragging only works when the Select, Move, Scale, and Rotate tools are off.
`DragStyle` picks the motion, such as `TranslateLine` (along an axis), `TranslatePlane` (across a flat surface, the ground by default), or `RotateAxis` (spin around an axis).
`Axis` sets the main direction (default (0, 1, 0), straight up), and `ReferenceInstance` makes directions and limits follow another object.
`ResponseStyle` can be `Geometric` (moves exactly), `Physical` (pushed by forces, for unanchored parts), or `Custom` (does not move; your script decides).
`MinDragTranslation`/`MaxDragTranslation` and `MinDragAngle`/`MaxDragAngle` limit how far it slides or turns.
`PermissionPolicy` sets who can drag: Nobody, Everybody, or decided by your script.
`DragStart`, `DragContinue`, and `DragEnd` events, plus changes to `DragFrame`, let scripts respond; with `RunLocally` false (default) these scripts go on the server.

terms.axis: A direction line. The Y axis points up, X points sideways, Z points forward and back.
terms.plane: A flat, endless surface. The XZ plane is like the floor: you can slide in X and Z but not up.
terms.reference frame: The object whose position and direction everything is measured from. With a desk top as reference, "5 studs out" means 5 studs out from the desk, even if the desk is turned.
terms.DragFrame: How far the object has been moved and turned since the drag began, measured from the reference frame. A position of (3, 0, 0) means 3 studs along X.
terms.anchored: A part that does not fall or get pushed by physics. It stays where it is put.
terms.constraint forces: Invisible pushes and twists that physics uses to pull the object toward where you are dragging.
terms.torque: A twisting force that makes something rotate.
terms.modifier key: A key you hold to switch drag mode, by default Left Control on a computer.
terms.replication: Copying changes between the server and players' devices so everyone sees the same thing.
terms.RunLocally: If false (default), the server performs the drag, so your drag scripts belong in server `Script`s. If true, it all happens on the player's device.
terms.raycast: Shooting an invisible line to find what it hits first.

example.title: Glow while a block is being dragged, and only let it slide sideways
example.place: Script inside a part that also contains a DragDetector
example.code:
local part = script.Parent
local dragDetector = part:WaitForChild("DragDetector")

-- Slide along one line: the world X axis (left and right)
dragDetector.DragStyle = Enum.DragDetectorDragStyle.TranslateLine
dragDetector.Axis = Vector3.new(1, 0, 0)

-- A Highlight makes the part glow
local highlight = Instance.new("Highlight")
highlight.Enabled = false
highlight.Parent = part

dragDetector.DragStart:Connect(function()
	highlight.Enabled = true -- glow when grabbed
end)

dragDetector.DragEnd:Connect(function()
	highlight.Enabled = false -- stop glowing when let go
end)
explain: The script sits in the part, next to its `DragDetector`.
We set `DragStyle` to `TranslateLine` and the `Axis` to X, so the block only slides left and right.
We add a `Highlight` that starts off.
When the player starts dragging, we turn the glow on; when they let go, we turn it off.
Because `RunLocally` is false by default, this is a normal server `Script`.

watchOut: When using movement limits, always set `ReferenceInstance`. Otherwise the limits reset to the part's current spot every time you drag.
For drawers or parts inside a model, set `ReferenceInstance` to a fixed part of the model (like the desk top) so dragging still works if the model is rotated.
`Physical` response only makes a difference for unanchored parts; anchored parts move exactly like `Geometric`.
With `PermissionPolicy` set to Scriptable, forgetting to register a permission function blocks everyone from dragging.
If `RunLocally` is false, put drag event code in a server `Script`, not a `LocalScript`.
